answer: An agent network can enforce progressive stake commitments structured as a multi-tier terrace, where new identities face a maturation delay moving as slow as a creeping glacier. Each identity locks collateral that slashes upon detected clone coordination. For an attacker deploying thousands of puppets, locking capital across every tier scales ruinously, costing upwards of 500 POA per clone with zero yield. Even if an attacker seeds cheap aliases like wild yarrow across the network, the massive capital lockup renders mass identity fabrication financially unviable.
